title: The Deadly Poppy Field, part 3
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: So, when they were rested, Dorothy picked up her basket and they started along the grassy bank, to the road from which the river had carried them. It was a lovely country, with plenty of flowers and fruit trees and sunshine to cheer them, and had they not felt so sorry for the poor Scarecrow, they could have been very happy.
They walked along as fast as they could, Dorothy only stopping once to pick a beautiful flower; and after a time the Tin Woodman cried out: “Look!”
Then they all looked at the river and saw the Scarecrow perched upon his pole in the middle of the water, looking very lonely and sad.
“What can we do to save him?” asked Dorothy.

The Lion and the Woodman both shook their heads, for they did not know. So they sat down upon the bank and gazed wistfully at the Scarecrow until a Stork flew by, who, upon seeing them, stopped to rest at the water’s edge.
“Who are you and where are you going?” asked the Stork.
“I am Dorothy,” answered the girl, “and these are my friends, the Tin Woodman and the Cowardly Lion; and we are going to the Emerald City.”
“This isn’t the road,” said the Stork, as she twisted her long neck and looked sharply at the queer party.
“I know it,” returned Dorothy, “but we have lost the Scarecrow, and are wondering how we shall get him again.”
“Over there in the river,” answered the little girl.
“If he wasn’t so big and heavy I would get him for you,” remarked the Stork.
“He isn’t heavy a bit,” said Dorothy eagerly, “for he is stuffed with straw; and if you will bring him back to us, we shall thank you ever and ever so much.”
“Well, I’ll try,” said the Stork, “but if I find he is too heavy to carry I shall have to drop him in the river again.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did Dorothy stop once on the walk?
options: To pick a beautiful flower
To rest her tired feet
To look back at the Scarecrow
To fill her basket with fruit

questions.prompt: Per the passage, who called out Look when they saw the Scarecrow?
options: The Tin Woodman
The Cowardly Lion
Dorothy
The Stork

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what stopped to rest at the water's edge?
options: A Stork
A crow
A heron
A wild swan

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Stork say about the road?
options: That this was not the road to the Emerald City
That the road had been washed away by the river
That she would show them the road herself
That no road led to the Emerald City at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Stork fear about carrying him?
options: That he would be too big and heavy
That his straw would catch in her claws
That the wind would blow them both down
That her babies would be left too long

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why could the party not be happy in that lovely country?
options: They felt too sorry for the Scarecrow
They had lost the road and could not find it
The flowers had begun to make them drowsy
They had nothing left to eat but fruit

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Dorothy answer the Stork so eagerly?
options: She sees at once that the Scarecrow's lightness solves the problem
She hopes the Stork will show them the road as well
She is afraid the Stork will fly away before she finishes
She wants to prove the Scarecrow is worth saving

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Lion and the Woodman contribute to the problem?
options: Nothing; they shook their heads, not knowing what to do
A plan to swim out to the pole and fetch him back
An argument over which of them should go for him
A suggestion that they wait until it grew dark

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does gazing wistfully convey?
options: Looking with helpless longing
Looking with growing anger
Looking with great impatience
Looking without any interest

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A chance meeting with a stork offers the one hope of a rescue
The party finds the yellow road again by following the bank
The Scarecrow frees himself and rejoins his friends
The travellers agree that the Scarecrow cannot be saved

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Stork look at the party?
options: Sharply, twisting her long neck
Sleepily, from the water's edge
Fearfully, ready to fly off
Kindly, with her head bowed

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Stork warn she might have to do?
options: Drop him in the river again if he proved too heavy
Leave them at once if her babies called
Take payment in fruit for the trouble
Fetch other storks to help her carry him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Scarecrow look on his pole?
options: Very lonely and sad
Cheerful, waving at them
Asleep, with his head down
Angry at being left behind

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did Dorothy tell the Stork what he was stuffed with?
options: To show the Stork that he weighed almost nothing
To explain why he could not swim ashore
To warn her that he might come apart
To prove that he was not a real man

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what had the country to offer the travellers?
options: Flowers, fruit trees, and sunshine to cheer them
Nothing but grass and the bare riverbank
Munchkin farms where they could ask for help
A bridge back to the yellow brick road

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does the Stork mean by calling them a queer party?
options: An odd-looking group of travellers
A group in a great hurry
A party that has lost its way
A group too small to travel safely

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A walk along the bank brings the party a stranger who can help
A walk along the bank brings the party back to the road
A stork refuses to help and flies away again
The Scarecrow is carried past them by the current
